channel.title: Eventually Consistent
channel.description: A daily bite-sized explainer of one systems/backend concept.
channel.itunes:summary: A daily bite-sized explainer of one systems/backend concept.
channel.itunes:author: Oakley Hall

item.title: Day 27: Failover
item.description: Failover: detect a dead primary, fence it, promote a standby, and redirect clients, plus the speed-versus-safety trade-off
item.itunes:summary: Failover: detect a dead primary, fence it, promote a standby, and redirect clients, plus the speed-versus-safety trade-off

item.title: Day 26: Split-brain
item.description: Split-brain: when a network partition leaves two active primaries writing conflicting truth, and how quorum and fencing prevent it
item.itunes:summary: Split-brain: when a network partition leaves two active primaries writing conflicting truth, and how quorum and fencing prevent it

item.title: Day 25: Hot partition
item.description: Hot partitions: when one shard takes all the heat and how systems cope
item.itunes:summary: Hot partitions: when one shard takes all the heat and how systems cope

item.title: Day 24: Data locality
item.description: Data locality: keep related data close to the code that uses it, and the latency trade-offs when you don't.
item.itunes:summary: Data locality: keep related data close to the code that uses it, and the latency trade-offs when you don't.

item.title: Day 23: Resharding
item.description: Resharding: changing shard count or shard key while the system keeps running, how online reshards work, and why cutover is the scary part.
item.itunes:summary: Resharding: changing shard count or shard key while the system keeps running, how online reshards work, and why cutover is the scary part.

item.title: Day 22: Rebalancing
item.description: How clusters move data between nodes as they grow, shrink, or get lopsided, and why eager rebalancing can turn a blip into an outage.
item.itunes:summary: How clusters move data between nodes as they grow, shrink, or get lopsided, and why eager rebalancing can turn a blip into an outage.

item.title: Day 21: Compaction
item.description: How LSM-tree databases merge old files, drop tombstones, and trade write, read, and space costs.
item.itunes:summary: How LSM-tree databases merge old files, drop tombstones, and trade write, read, and space costs.

item.title: Day 20: Checkpointing
item.description: Checkpointing: how databases flush dirty pages and mark a safe point in the log so crash recovery stays fast and old log segments can be recycled.
item.itunes:summary: Checkpointing: how databases flush dirty pages and mark a safe point in the log so crash recovery stays fast and old log segments can be recycled.

item.title: Day 19: Write-ahead logging (WAL)
item.description: Write-ahead logging: why databases write changes to an append-only log before touching data, and how that log powers crash recovery, replication and point-in-time restore.
item.itunes:summary: Write-ahead logging: why databases write changes to an append-only log before touching data, and how that log powers crash recovery, replication and point-in-time restore.

item.title: Day 18: Three-phase commit (3PC)
item.description: Three-phase commit adds a pre-commit step to avoid 2PC blocking, but breaks under network partitions.
item.itunes:summary: Three-phase commit adds a pre-commit step to avoid 2PC blocking, but breaks under network partitions.

item.title: Day 17: Two-phase commit (2PC)
item.description: Two-phase commit: how a coordinator gets several databases to vote, then commit or abort together, and why it blocks when the coordinator crashes.
item.itunes:summary: Two-phase commit: how a coordinator gets several databases to vote, then commit or abort together, and why it blocks when the coordinator crashes.

item.title: Day 16: MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control)
item.description: MVCC: how databases keep multiple row versions so readers never block writers, and the cleanup cost that comes with it.
item.itunes:summary: MVCC: how databases keep multiple row versions so readers never block writers, and the cleanup cost that comes with it.

item.title: Day 15: Snapshot isolation
item.description: Snapshot isolation: consistent reads from a frozen view of the database, and the write skew trap
item.itunes:summary: Snapshot isolation: consistent reads from a frozen view of the database, and the write skew trap

item.title: Day 14: Strong consistency
item.description: Strong consistency: every read sees the latest write, and what that costs in latency and availability
item.itunes:summary: Strong consistency: every read sees the latest write, and what that costs in latency and availability

item.title: Day 13: Eventual consistency
item.description: Eventual consistency: replicas converge over time, trading fresh reads for speed and availability.
item.itunes:summary: Eventual consistency: replicas converge over time, trading fresh reads for speed and availability.

item.title: Day 12: ACID
item.description: ACID: the four transaction guarantees, the write-ahead log, and why isolation levels still matter
item.itunes:summary: ACID: the four transaction guarantees, the write-ahead log, and why isolation levels still matter

item.title: Day 11: BASE
item.description: BASE: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent, the availability-first alternative to ACID and what it costs your app.
item.itunes:summary: BASE: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent, the availability-first alternative to ACID and what it costs your app.

item.title: Day 10: CAP theorem
item.description: CAP theorem: when the network splits, you choose consistency or availability, and PACELC adds latency to the everyday picture.
item.itunes:summary: CAP theorem: when the network splits, you choose consistency or availability, and PACELC adds latency to the everyday picture.

item.title: Day 9: Consensus
item.description: How Raft and Paxos get a cluster to agree on one answer, why etcd stops writes without a majority, and what that costs.
item.itunes:summary: How Raft and Paxos get a cluster to agree on one answer, why etcd stops writes without a majority, and what that costs.

item.title: Day 8: Quorum
item.description: Quorums: how R plus W greater than N lets replicated databases tolerate failures and still read recent writes.
item.itunes:summary: Quorums: how R plus W greater than N lets replicated databases tolerate failures and still read recent writes.

item.title: Day 7: Multi-leader replication
item.description: Multi-leader replication: several nodes accept writes for low-latency multi-region and offline use, at the cost of resolving write conflicts.
item.itunes:summary: Multi-leader replication: several nodes accept writes for low-latency multi-region and offline use, at the cost of resolving write conflicts.

item.title: Day 6: Leader–Follower replication
item.description: Leader–follower replication: one writer, followers copy the log, lag and failover trade-offs.
item.itunes:summary: Leader–follower replication: one writer, followers copy the log, lag and failover trade-offs.

item.title: Day 5: Read replicas
item.description: Read replicas: scale SELECTs off the primary, and live with replication lag.
item.itunes:summary: Read replicas: scale SELECTs off the primary, and live with replication lag.

item.title: Day 4: Normalization
item.description: Store each fact once: normal forms one through three, an orders and customers example, and the join-cost trade-off.
item.itunes:summary: Store each fact once: normal forms one through three, an orders and customers example, and the join-cost trade-off.
